answer: Because the karst fee is applied at the cedar exit, the kernel audit totals the burn and the ledger exposes exactly what left. Withdrawing stake burns a 1% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. An operator rotating funds across many keys thus bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. That is 23 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
